title: The same trap in a different suit

feedback.title: Save the king; the ace is already gone
feedback.summary: East has already shown void in Clubs and is free to trump this trick with any heart no matter which Club you play; playing the low card avoids exposing your king to that known void, keeping its winning potential for later instead of spending it here.
points: The earlier trick shows East playing a diamond when Clubs were led, so East holds no more Clubs this hand and is free to trump this one.
The ace of Clubs is already out, so the king is the highest Club left — it keeps genuine winning potential once it is not exposed to East's known void.
The target still needs one more trick from the two remaining; this avoids spending the king on a trick East controls, without giving up on it.

feedback.title: Risking your best card on a trick you don't control
feedback.summary: East's confirmed void means East decides whether this trick is trumped, regardless of which Club you play, so leading with the king exposes your best remaining card to that known void for a trick you don't control.
points: The earlier trick already showed East void in Clubs — East can trump this trick with any heart no matter which Club you offer.
If East trumps, the king is spent for nothing, and only the weak four is left for the final trick the target still needs.
The four loses this trick just as surely as a trumped king would, but keeps the king in hand as a genuine option for later.

author_notes: Third void-tracking scenario (EC-042). A second, independent example of the same 'preserve your master card against a known void' pattern from play_void_tracking_001, with a different seat, suit and trump to reinforce pattern recognition rather than a single memorized case.
